note.markdown:
# Revenue and retention brief: October

## ARR
ARR closed October at $15.49M, up from $15.25M. New ARR of $319.7k and expansion of $113.4k outweighed churn of $133.8k and contraction of $54.5k.

## Retention
Net revenue retention is 98.0% overall, down from 101.7% in June, and gross retention is 90.3%. The decline is concentrated in SMB, where NRR fell to 87.4% from 96.4% and gross retention is 80.4%. SMB contraction from July to October totals $173.0k of ARR, against $34.3k from March to June. That timing is consistent with the July packaging change. Billing shows the seat reductions but not the reason, so it is worth confirming with the SMB team. Mid-market (102.7%) and Enterprise (104.3%) remain above 100%.

## Billing exceptions
Three closed-won deals in HubSpot have no subscription in billing: Granite Clinics West ($52.0k), Summit Couriers ($38.5k) and Willow Dental Group ($12.6k), together $103.1k of ARR that is not yet counted. Blue Couriers Co is billed at $66.9k against an $83.6k deal, $16.7k short.

## Renewals at risk
There are 8 accounts with $728.6k of ARR at risk: 6 high and 2 medium.
- **Halcyon Health** ($197.3k): active users per seat are down 35.6%, with 16 support tickets in the last month against 3.3 a month before, mostly integration errors.
- **North Labs Systems** ($183.2k, renewing first): usage is down 40.2%, with 12 tickets against 3.7 a month before.
- **Four mid-market accounts at high risk:** Maple Clinics Holdings ($69.7k), North Schools Group ($68.8k), Blue Staffing Systems ($52.0k) and Copper Dental Systems ($50.3k). Usage is down between 33.9% and 40.1%, and support tickets have jumped.
- **Pine Group and Harbor Foods Collective (medium):** usage is down 34.3% and 34.4%, with normal ticket volume.

## For discussion
- Whether to review the July packaging change for SMB, given the contraction since then.
- Who creates the three missing subscriptions and corrects the Blue Couriers Co amount.
- Executive calls with Halcyon Health and North Labs Systems before their renewals. Integration errors lead the tickets at most at-risk accounts: is there a common cause?
